newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Old Mutual sees boom phase for small firms.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Old Mutual sees boom phase for small firms.

text.p: South Africa's largest investment group Old Mutual on Thursday announced the launch of a small companies' growth fund ahead of an expected explosion in small company growth this year.
The fund, to be launched on May 2, would focus on emerging financial and industrial companies with market capitalisation below 1.5 billion rand, fund manager Brendan Burgess told a news briefing.
It would only invest in shares which fell outside the "top 100 companies" in the country -- representing 446 counters worth around 178 billion rand or 17 percent of the market.

Bryan Hopkins, head of research at Old Mutual Asset Managers said he expected a steady flow of new listings on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) during the course of the year and company earnings to accelerate sharply.
"Small companies have entered a boom phase in the democratic South Africa," Hopkins said.

The improved business climate, as well as the fact that several small firms were niche players in their markets and therefore less reliant on the overall economic growth rate, would bolster earnings, he said.
Small companies' expansion into other sub-Saharan African countries would also be to their benefit, he added.
Hopkins said Old Mutual had already invested more than 13 billion rand in small firms on the JSE and participated in several rights issues to raise capital.

By the end of this month the JSE -- ranked the world's 13th biggest bourse at end-February by number of companies listed -- will have seen eight debut listings in 1997, just ahead of the seven recorded in the same period last year.
At least another six firms, active in a wide range of sectors including electronics, mining and horse racing are gearing up to come to the South African market in the next few months.
